articles.title: Deputy FBI director reportedly plans to retire after less than a year on the job
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) - Christopher Raia, the FBI's deputy director, intends to retire in ‌December, the Washington Post reported on ‌Monday, citing three people familiar with the matter, marking ​the latest departure from the bureau during the Trump administration. The FBI and the US Department of Justice did not immediately respond to a ‌request for comment. Raia, ⁠a longtime FBI career official, was tapped in January to replace right-wing ⁠podcaster and former Secret Service agent Dan Bongino, who was regarded as unconventional pick for ​the role. Before ​this role, Raia was ​assistant director in ‌charge of the New York Field Office and has been with the FBI since 2003, previously serving as a top counterterrorism official. Major personnel changes have taken place at the FBI during ‌Trump's second term in ​which political experts have raised ​concerns over ​the president's use of federal probes ‌to go after political opponents ​and critics. The ​Trump administration has seen some personnel changes across agencies since Republicans suffered defeats in ​the US ‌midterm elections in November. articles.title: Trump blasts Newsom's death penalty commutations as 'shocking act of injustice'
articles.summary: President Donald Trump listens as Sandy Friend speaks about her late son Michael Lyons, at the Department of Justice in Washington on Nov. 23, 2026.  (Mark Schiefelbein/AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein) WASHINGTON - President Donald Trump blasted Gov. Gavin Newsom's decision to commute every death sentence in California , calling the move "one of the most shocking acts of injustice our country has ever seen" at a Monday press conference with victims' family members at the Department of Justice. Trump said he "couldn't believe" Newsom's choice to commute the sentences of some of California's most notorious serial killers and rapists. He used a good portion of the event to describe in great detail some of the murders that landed the 548 condemned people in California on death row, specifically mentioning Charles Ng, who was convicted of murdering nine adults and two children in 1984-85, Randy Kraft, a serial murderer known in the 1970s and ‘80s as the "Scorecard Killer" and Robert Boyd Rhoades, who brutally raped, tortured and killed 8-year-old Michael Lyons in 1996, among others. "You'd have to read their biographies to see how bad they were. Some of them you wouldn't even believe," Trump said, calling Newsom a "terrible governor." "He stood with the murderers and the child slayers," he said. "But today we say the American people stand with you." Trump's press conference seemed designed as much to politically whack Newsom over the commutations as it was to honor victims, representing the latest chapter in the years-long feud between the two men who have regularly sparred during their overlapping time in office over crime and punishment. Newsom, for his part, said his commutations decision, which he announced earlier this month, was inspired in part by a national reckoning over the death penalty, including a botched execution in Tennessee and a Trump administration announcement - later walked back - that it planned to livestream a federal execution by a firing squad. Newsom slammed Trump in a video he posted just before the press conference, calling out the president for what he claimed was blatant hypocrisy. He said Trump has used his post to pardon numerous criminals, including those with close ties to the president or his allies. Trump also granted widespread clemency to nearly all of the Jan. 6 defendants , many of whom went on to reoffend . "Donald Trump doesn't oppose mercy. He sells it," Newsom said. "If you are poor, Black or brown, you get the needle. If you are rich and know Donald Trump, you get a pardon and a personal phone call." Newsom noted that in 1989, Trump called for the death penalty for the so-called Central Park Five, or the five Black and Latino teenagers who were wrongfully convicted of raping a white woman in the park. "They were innocent, DNA proved it, you never apologized," Newsom said. Both Newsom and Trump have touted crime statistics to promote their agendas and policy priorities. Trump said during the event that " crime rates have gone down 84%," though it was unclear what specific crimes he was referencing or if it was an overall national or local trend. Newsom's office has in recent weeks also touted lower crimes in California, including a "record low" homicide rate . Trump's event underscores the intense scrutiny and political backlash that has surrounded Newsom since he made his decision, which already faces at least one legal challenge and that in some cases must be reviewed under state law by the California Supreme Court. But the president's choice to orchestrate such a major event to publicly admonish a governor's decision is unusual, said Erwin Chemerinsky, dean of UC Berkeley Law School. "I do not recall a president ever attempting to undermine a governor's commuting of death sentences," Chemerinsky said in an email. "Other governors have done this, but to my knowledge, no president ever has done this before." That's in part because, however controversial, governors have legal jurisdiction over state commutations so Trump has little, if any, power to stop Newsom's action. "This is a publicity stunt by the president, not a serious legal effort," Chemerinsky said. Several family members of victims also spoke at the event, during which they celebrated Trump and ridiculed Newsom. "Michael was 8 years old. He loved his sisters, fishing, Ninja Turtles, telling campfire stories and bringing me flowers. Michael was afraid of the dark. He believed the boogeyman was going to get him," his mother, Sandy Friend said, battling tears. Friend said the night her son was killed, "Michael learned that the boogeyman was real." She said Newsom, with the swipe of a pen and without notifying families, "erased" justice for her son's killer. "You took the only justice we had and let families feel abandoned by the state that promised to protect us," she said. "You'll never understand the unimaginable pain that you're putting these families through. Face me, Governor Newsom. Tell me Michael's life doesn't matter." Newsom was careful to focus his criticism on Trump and did not use the video to explain his decision or undermine victims' grief. In an open letter to Californians announcing the commutations, Newsom said he agonized over it for years and ultimately made his choice over a firm belief that "state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California's values." He also told the Chronicle in an interview earlier this month that he made the choice after speaking with the sisters of Polly Klaas , a 12-year-old who was abducted from her home in Petaluma in 1993 and brutally killed. The man convicted of murdering her was sentenced to death and is still alive. "This decision was not made by a jury. It was not approved by the voters. It was made by one politician acting alone," Marc Klaas, Polly's father, said at the event. "While nothing can bring Polly back, her life mattered. The pain inflicted on our family was real." Newsom acknowledged the families who joined Trump's press conference to denounce the commutations in his Monday video. "To the families standing with him today, your grief is real," he said. "That's why every person, every person, on California's former death row will die in prison. No one walks out. Donald Trump's criminals? They walk out." Speculation had swirled for weeks that Newsom would commute the sentences before he leaves office in January and before launching an expected 2028 presidential bid. The decision could help Newsom earn support from the more progressive wing of his party in what's expected to be a crowded Democratic primary field, but it could also hobble his odds against more law-and-order candidates who appeal to anti-MAGA Republicans and swing voters. The White House emphasized that California voters have repeatedly rejected efforts to overturn the death penalty, including as early as 2016, when they voted against a ballot measure to ban it and passed another to speed up executions, part of which was later invalidated by the courts. National support for the death penalty also remains strong. A July 2026 survey by the Pew Research Center found that two-thirds of American adults support capital punishment for people convicted of murder, including 51% of Democrats and 84% of Republicans. Trump touted an executive order he signed on his first day back in office "restoring the death penalty" after former President Joe Biden commuted the sentences of 37 people on federal death row during his last days in office. Trump also announced Monday he would sign a directive "ordering the Department of Justice to seek the death penalty for child murderers, as well as rapists and human traffickers who kill their victims," adding that the order would also "expedite the execution of federal death sentences." It's unclear how or whether the order would affect California and Newsom's commutations, which are within his jurisdiction as governor. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for clarification. Trump also said Rep. Brandon Gill, R-Texas, would introduce a bill to "strengthen the death penalty in America." "And it's going to be much different than it was in the past," Trump said. "It's going to be strong and it'll be swift." Natasha Minsker, a lobbyist who has worked with a coalition of anti-death penalty advocates urging Newsom to commute the sentences, slammed Trump for using the death penalty for "political purposes" in a way that doesn't help victims or their families. "It is once again prosecutors and politicians using the death penalties to bring attention to themselves and for their own political gain and with no eye to what's in the best interest of the families and with no interest to what actually protects our communities and keeps us safe," she said. "This is a state law issue. This is about whether people in California support the governor, and it's about the governor's ability to commute under the state Constitution." articles.title: Storms could disrupt Thanksgiving flights as San Francisco braces for record tides
articles.summary: Millions of Americans hitting the road and skies for Thanksgiving could run into storms on both coasts, including one that could last through Thanksgiving Day. Forecasters are tracking a developing nor'easter on the East Coast that could bring heavy rain, gusty winds and coastal flooding to the Southeast starting Wednesday before moving north into the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast on Thanksgiving Day. "Ahead of the storm, the eastern U.S. will be mainly dry on Monday and Tuesday, allowing a favorable travel window," according to Dan DePodwin, AccuWeather vice president of forecast operations. "A significant deterioration in the weather is expected starting Tuesday night across the Southeast and then spreading northward along and east of the Appalachians Wednesday through Friday." On the West Coast, forecasters are monitoring a few storms fueled by an atmospheric river that could disrupt travel before, during and after the Thanksgiving holiday, according to AccuWeather . "Each of these storms has the potential to trigger major weather delays at major Northeast and West Coast hubs," the Weather Channel said . Weather hasn't been the only problem facing travelers. Delta Air Lines resolved an outage that caused delays nationwide Sunday, marking the third major disruption to U.S. air travel in nine days. AAA projects that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Tuesday, Nov. 24, and Monday, Nov. 30, including 72.9 million by car and 5.96 million on domestic flights. Tuesday and Wednesday: Atmospheric river in the West, storms in the Southeast Map of atmospheric river forecast to affect California leading up to Thanksgiving Day. AccuWeather A strong Pacific storm is forecast to hit from Northern California to Washington state starting Tuesday, with rain reaching the Northwest Monday night. The greatest impacts are expected Tuesday and Wednesday, with a risk of flooding and mudslides. Heavy rain, strong winds and mountain snow could cause significant delays along Interstate 5 between Seattle and San Francisco and on mountain routes including I-80. Airports in Seattle and San Francisco could see delays. "Drivers along I-5 should prepare for heavy rain that can reduce visibility and leave water collecting on the roadway," AccuWeather meteorologist Haley Taylor said. "Travelers heading into the Sierra will face a different challenge, with heavy snow potentially making mountain routes difficult or impassable." A second, potentially windier storm could strike the same area Wednesday, with the heaviest rain spreading to most of the West Coast on Thursday, the Weather Channel said. The National Weather Service office in Reno said the storms will bring fresh snow to the Sierra Nevada, with periods of difficult travel. In the San Francisco Bay Area, the storms coincide with potentially record-breaking king tides, the year's highest tides. The National Weather Service has a coastal flood warning in effect until 4 p.m. PT Thursday and calls Tuesday and Wednesday an "extreme" risk for flooding along the bay shoreline, and a high surf warning covers Wednesday on the Pacific coast. The agency said the storm will coincide with the king tides, potentially making flooding worse during Thanksgiving travel. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie said Sunday city departments are coordinating and "deploying resources" for the storms and high tides. He previously warned of potentially record tides in an X post Saturday. "We went through the forecast for next week, and we are anticipating high tides and rain that this city has never seen before," he said. "This is extremely serious, and we are acting accordingly at the city level. We are going to encourage every resident and business owner to take this extremely seriously. In Marin County, Southern Marin Fire District has urged residents and businesses to "take action now" and prepare for possible road closures and travel disruptions. In the Southeast, heavy rain and thunderstorms could hit Atlanta and Charlotte on Wednesday, one of the busiest travel days of the year. AccuWeather said Wednesday could bring some of the most widespread weather-related travel disruptions before Thanksgiving, particularly in the Southeast, with airline delays expected to expand in Orlando and Miami from Tuesday to Wednesday and in Atlanta and Charlotte on Wednesday. The National Weather Service's Weather Prediction Center has warned of flooding rain along the coastal Carolinas on Wednesday. Delays at those hubs could ripple across the country. Thanksgiving Day: Possible major storm in the Northeast Forecasters are increasingly confident that another storm will form off the Southeast coast late Wednesday and move up the East Coast on Thanksgiving, bringing heavy rain and strong winds from the mid-Atlantic to New England. "Strong winds and heavy rain could lead to thousands of airport delays, especially on Thanksgiving Day in the mid-Atlantic and Northeast," said DePodwin. The National Weather Service in Boston called it a "potentially significant coastal storm" for Thanksgiving into Friday, with gusts along the coast possibly topping 50 mph. Very high tides could also bring coastal flooding, the agency said. Interior parts of the Northeast and the Appalachians could see some snow or ice. The storm arrives as king tides continue on both coasts around Tuesday's full moon, which could worsen coastal flooding, the Weather Channel said. Interior parts of the Northeast and the Appalachians could see some snow or ice. AccuWeather said a brief period of wet snow or sleet is possible in northern New York and New England later Thursday. That could be a problem for the 1 00th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York, which is set to start at 8:30 a.m. Thursday . The parade's giant balloons can't fly if sustained winds top 23 mph or gusts top 34 mph, Fox Weather reported . Forecasters say the storm's exact track and timing could still shift. The weekend after Thanksgiving The National Weather Service expects the East Coast storm to weaken and move away, though windy conditions and some rain or snow showers could linger in parts of New England and the eastern Great Lakes into the weekend. Another storm could form in the East during the busy return weekend, while more Pacific storms could hit the West Coast. The Sunday after Thanksgiving is typically one of the busiest travel days of the year. Forecasters advise travelers to check forecasts for both their departure and arrival cities, and to keep an eye on flight status before heading to the airport. articles.title: Nvidia pulls a U-turn and reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, rocketing its stock
articles.summary: Nvidia's ( NVDA ) stock rocketed more than 30% Monday after the company's board announced it reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and president of the chip giant. The chip giant added nearly $1 trillion to its market cap, posting its best day since May 2023. Shares of neoclouds CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius ( NBIS ) also climbed more than 30%. In a statement Monday, Nvidia’s board said it had a series of discussions with Huang and was satisfied with his candor and ability to lead the company. "The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said. Follow live updates and reactions to Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO > FILE PHOTO: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang speaks at event ahead of the COMPUTEX forum, in Taipei, Taiwan June 2, 2024. REUTERS/Ann Wang/File Photo Reuters / REUTERS "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's CFO," he added. Jones will remain the chair of Nvidia's board. Just last week, Jones told investors during the company's Q3 earnings call that Nvidia had no plans to bring back Huang. Huang resigned from Nvidia on Nov. 12 after an alleged affair with Alice Huang, suspected of being a Chinese spy. Huang admitted to having an affair at the time but didn't name the woman. He also allegedly had affairs with two Nvidia employees, including executive Kimberly Powell. Alice Huang was the executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is suspected of  smuggling high-powered Nvidia chips to China. The company said the board received input from senior levels of the US government and, based on that input, doesn't believe Huang's reinstatement poses a national security risk. "I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement. "I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry, and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can't wait to get back to work," he added. Jensen Huang's allies, including President Trump, reportedly lobbied for his return as CEO. In a Truth Social post, Trump lauded Huang's reinstatement. "The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy," Trump said. "The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct," Trump continued, adding he considers Huang a "Great Patriot and National Treasure." articles.title: White House staffer reportedly reveals Smithsonian overhaul plans by accident
articles.summary: (AFP via Getty) The Trump administration's plans for the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History were accidentally discovered by a commuter on a Washington Metro train last month. A commuter spotted a document titled "Smithsonian Institution Renewal Plan" displayed on a staffer's laptop, snapped photos, and sent them to ProPublica, the outlet reported . The list includes 25 items, including firing the museum's director, Anthea Hartig, and several top administrators and curators; installing a new permanent exhibit called "The Riches of Our Western Civilization Inheritance;" creating an exhibit on "Great Families of American History;" and announcing a new "colossus statue" of George Washington for the museum's entrance. The plan also calls for new guidelines for interpreting exhibits and a review of the Smithsonian's strategy for traveling exhibitions, including blocking one underway called "The Bias Inside Us." The Smithsonian's financial grants to "woke third parties" would also be reviewed, and its online K-12 curriculum would be overhauled to "realign educational materials with patriotism, not ideology." The plan appears to be a work in progress. The staffer also wrote down other proposals on a sheet of paper in plain view, according to ProPublica. The outlet identified the staffer as Sam Bock, a 27-year-old associate policy adviser with the Domestic Policy Council, the White House office that produced the July report. The White House did not respond to ProPublica's request for comment. The Trump administration has been at odds with the Smithsonian since the president's second term began. President Donald Trump issued an executive order in July directing the Interior Department, through the National Park Service, to install temporary signs along sidewalks and walkways leading to the museum, warning visitors that the museum does not accurately present U.S. history. The order said the signs "shall notify visitors that the Museum exhibits should be renovated consistent with the findings in the Report and direct visitors to locations and resources for accurate information regarding America's history." Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch announced his resignation in September. The Smithsonian operates outside the executive branch, and museum directors report to the secretary, who is subject to oversight by a board of regents that includes Vice President JD Vance, Chief Justice John Roberts, a bipartisan group of lawmakers, and citizen regents. articles.title: Congress reacts to Jensen Huang's reinstatement amid national security concerns
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — Members of Congress responded with swift, bipartisan fury Monday over the Nvidia board's surprise decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang at the behest of President Donald Trump , opening a new phase of questions about the chipmaking giant and potential national security lapses. Sen. Tim Scott, the outgoing Republican chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, announced that Huang will testify publicly before the panel on Dec. 3. Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the incoming chair, said the Trump administration needs to explain what role U.S. officials played in what she called a “reckless” decision. Rep. Robert Garcia, the incoming chairman of the House oversight committee, said Trump’s direct involvement with Nvidia’s decision-making “raises serious national security and corruption questions.” “We must investigate these actions,” said Garcia of California. Nvidia was already facing sharp scrutiny from Congress after Huang acknowledged a relationship with a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. officials believed to be a spy. Putting Huang back in charge, after Trump said the board did “what we wanted them to do,” raised stark concerns over the administration's role in the company that is central to the AI economy . As Democrats prepare to take charge of Congress in January, they are mounting investigations into the Trump administration, particularly Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who has close ties with the company. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent earlier this month said he was frustrated by the Commerce Department's delay in placing restrictions on Nvidia chip exports to Megaspeed, the company whose CEO, Alice Huang, was involved with Jensen Huang. "The controversy with Nvidia and Megaspeed is just the tip of the iceberg, and it’s not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back,” said Sen. Tom Cotton of Arkansas, the Republican chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee. “Congress has much to investigate,” he said. Huang is expected to appear for two days of interviews with three House committees next week, along with his public hearing at the Senate panel. “The NVIDIA board’s brief internal investigation and reinstatement of Jensen Huang do not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed," said a joint statement from Rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., chairman of the House Select Committee on China; Rep. Rick Crawford, R-Ark., chairman of the House Intelligence Committee; and Rep. Brian Mast, R-Fla., chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee. "We remain committed to getting answers on the mass smuggling of NVIDIA products, their diversion for Chinese military purposes, and their key role in advancing our foremost adversary’s AI capabilities.” At issue is the sale of chips to China Of concern to Congress is whether Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable publicly traded companies, has been selling its chips to China, in violation of export controls as the U.S. tries to protect certain technology that is at the core of the AI race. Earlier this year, members of Congress urged the U.S. Commerce Department to “suspend or reconsider” Nvidia's export licenses to China and to conduct a full national security review, according to a release earlier this month from Warren and a key Republican on the Senate banking committee, Sen. Jim Banks of Indiana. “Since then, NVIDIA has reportedly received approvals to export hundreds of thousands of advanced AI chips to China, including to companies tied to China’s military, all while attempting to influence the debate over chip controls in Washington, D.C.,” they wrote in a statement in November. “NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s confirmation of a relationship with a suspected spy for China’s intelligence service makes these national security concerns even more urgent and raises important questions NVIDIA must answer,” the two senators said. Republicans and Democrats are demanding answers While Republican leaders were mostly quiet on Huang’s return to Nvidia, other Republicans spoke more forcefully Monday. Texas Sen. John Cornyn, who lost his seat after Trump endorsed his GOP primary opponent, questioned the company’s comment that the U.S. said there was no security risk. “No national security risk? Based on what?” Cornyn posted. Cornyn asked whether the FBI did a defensive briefing of Huang to conclude there was no risk, “If not, why not?” Nebraska Rep. Don Bacon wrote on social media that the U.S. cannot say it wants to win the AI competition and then give China its best technology. “Congress needs to get to the bottom of who approved high end computer chips sales to China,” wrote Bacon, who is retiring from Congress. Ahead of the announcement but after Trump’s call for Huang to be reinstated, Republican Rep. Bill Huizenga of Michigan, who lost reelection to a Democrat, posted: “Ummm… she was, and is, a spy. How about we get serious about making sure China doesn’t steal US company technology?” Utah Sen. John Curtis asked similar questions. “Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board?” Curtis asked. “And on what basis did the board conclude there was no risk?” Democrats add to their anti-corruption agenda Democrats are preparing to dive more deeply into questions of national security and political corruption in Washington as they take over the committee gavels in January. “The guy who was having an affair with a Chinese spy while working relentlessly to help China get access to as many AI chips as possible? Really?” posted Delaware Sen. Chris Coons, who is poised to become the chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee when Democrats take the majority. Arizona Sen. Ruben Gallego, a Democrat, said that Congress should investigate “what stock positions took place before the announcement.” Oregon Sen. Ron Wyden, who will chair the Senate finance committee and serves on the Senate intelligence committee, said Huang's restatement shows that under Trump and his administration, “our national security is for sale.” “In January, Democrats will hold this corrupt administration accountable,” Wyden said. ___ Associated Press writers Kevin Freking, Aamer Madhani, Joey Cappelletti and Chris Rugaber contributed to this report. articles.title: Rep. Jimmy Gomez to resign after House panel finds evidence of sexual misconduct
articles.summary: Rep. Jimmy Gomez of Los Angeles said he would step down next week after the House ethics committee said it had evidence that he had engaged in sexual misconduct. He lost his reelection bid this month to Angela Gonzales-Torres by nearly 25 percentage points. (Heather Diehl / Getty Images) U.S. Rep. Jimmy Gomez, the Los Angeles Democrat, said Monday he would resign from Congress on Dec. 1 after a House investigation found credible evidence that he had engaged in sexual misconduct. There is “substantial evidence” that Gomez made unwanted sexual advances toward a female House staffer and violated the chamber’s rules, the House Ethics Committee said in a report Monday , concluding an investigation that began earlier this year. Gomez, 51, who was unseated in this month’s midterm elections, was accused by the former congressional staffer, a woman in her mid-20s, of two nonconsensual encounters. He has previously denied nonconsensual conduct. She told congressional investigators that in one instance, Gomez put his hand down her skirt while they were sitting on stools at a Washington bar and penetrated her; in the other, she said Gomez was “forceful” in an attempt to kiss her in his congressional office, according to the report. The committee found that Gomez’s conduct constituted sexual misconduct in violation of House rules and said his behavior “could constitute” sexual assault at a criminal misdemeanor level under Washington statutes. No legal charges have been brought against him. “Representative Gomez failed in his obligation to behave in a manner that reflects creditably on the House, and his conduct was exacerbated by his failure to appreciate the inherent power imbalance between House Members and House staff,” the committee said in the report. Read more: Allegations against Rep. Jimmy Gomez fuel momentum for DSA-backed challenger Gonzales-Torres Gomez, a married five-term congressman, said in a statement that he disagreed with the committee’s conclusions and accused it of “deficiencies” in the report, but said he would step down. He had previously acknowledged mistakes but maintained that his actions did not violate the law or House rules. “I recognize the seriousness of the Ethics Committee’s report and as I previously stated I take full responsibility for the personal mistakes I committed outside of my marriage,” he said. Attorneys for the former staffer applauded the committee’s work Monday. “Democracy cannot function properly when women must endure harassment and abuse as a condition of public service,” said lawyers Lisa J. Banks and Sara E. Nesbitt of the Washington-based firm Katz Banks Kumin. Gomez is the third male lawmaker this year, and the second California Democrat, to resign following allegations of sexual misconduct, following former Reps. Eric Swalwell (D-Dublin) and Tony Gonzales (R-Texas). Swalwell resigned in April after being accused of misconduct by several women, including a former staffer who alleged rape. Gonzales, who had previously admitted to having an affair with an aide who later died by suicide, immediately came under renewed scrutiny and also resigned. Within days, a report emerged accusing Gomez of kissing a congressional aide at a party hosted by Swalwell. The House Ethics Committee was reported to be investigating Gomez in June and formally announced its inquiry in August. Days later, attorneys representing the former staffer released a statement accusing Gomez of sexual assault. Gomez pursued reelection but was defeated this month by Democrat Angela Gonzales-Torres. Following his loss, his term was set to expire at the end of the year. On Monday, Gonzales-Torres criticized Gomez for not resigning sooner. The accusations against him, she said, “reflect a broader environment of sexual misconduct and toxic working conditions on Capitol Hill.” His resignation will leave some Angelenos without federal representation for a month; Gonzales-Torres said she would work with other elected officials so constituents in the East and Central Los Angeles congressional district do not feel the gap in services. Gomez said his staff would work to close out constituent casework by Dec. 1. According to the report, the House committee interviewed the former staffer, who detailed the alleged incident at the Washington bar in February 2024. The two were at a birthday party for another member of Congress, who was dating a woman in a relationship that was not public. Gomez and the staffer first met there; both were “chaperoning” the other couple. Around 11 p.m., the four of them moved to a different bar. There, Gomez and the staffer began talking; she told investigators he complimented her looks. He described their conversation as “flirting.” As they sat on barstools, Gomez put his hand down her skirt, the staffer alleged. She said she ran to the bathroom, where she began to cry, then retrieved her purse and left the bar. Gomez met her outside, where she told the committee he kissed her against a wall. She said she  kissed him back because she “wanted it to just end and just give him what he wanted … so that we can go home.” The committee reported that Gomez first said that he had only engaged in consensual kissing with the woman, but later testified that he made sexual contact with her only outside the bar and after asking for her permission. In his statement Monday, Gomez cast doubt on the committee’s investigatory process, accusing it of having “selectively quoted, disparaged, and disregarded” his statements and complaining that he was not given a chance to respond to the final report. The staffer said the second instance occurred in July 2024. She said she was at a happy hour on Capitol Hill during an evening vote series when she texted Gomez; she said she did not remember why. Gomez invited her to his office. There, Gomez told the committee that they discussed her dating life. He said she told him she did not “want to do anything here” and he said OK. Read more: Swalwell scandal sparks fears of deeper rot on Capitol Hill The staffer said she became uncomfortable after Gomez commented about a reporter on the television, calling the reporter “hot” and saying he texted her frequently. She said she went to the door and they said goodbye, but that as she opened the door, Gomez grabbed her arm and tried to kiss her. She said no and tried to push him off, then ran out once she succeeded. She testified that Gomez was “forceful” during the encounter. Gomez told the committee that he gave her “a beso, a kiss on the cheek, a hug, and she left” and did not otherwise touch her. He said she did not resist or appear uncomfortable. The staffer’s attorneys said Gomez destroyed the young woman’s dreams of a career in public service. They said further steps should be taken by Congress to address the “toxic and predatory” workplace culture described in the report. “She sacrificed her own sense of safety and privacy to help reveal the ongoing misogyny and debauchery that permeates Capitol Hill,” Banks and Nesbitt said. “Representative Gomez seems to believe that the power he wields, both as a man and as a member of Congress, makes him untouchable. Today’s findings are a meaningful step toward dismantling that belief.” During the investigation, Gomez also disclosed a past “consensual, sexual relationship” with a second woman, a senior employee in another Congress member’s office. That woman told the committee she had never had a nonconsensual encounter with Gomez. Gomez was ousted by Gonzales-Torres by a nearly 25-percentage-point margin in this month’s election. The sexual misconduct allegations levied against him fueled momentum for her campaign, which was partly built around accountability and ethics in government. “We’re going to take on this apparent culture in Congress in which men appear to abuse their positions of power and abuse women and younger staffers,” Gonzales-Torres said on left-wing streamer Hasan Piker’s show in October. articles.title: Trump says Huang is not a national security risk. Why are others so concerned?
articles.summary: When news broke Monday that Nvidia had reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO less than two weeks after he resigned amid reports of multiple extramarital affairs — including one with a woman suspected of spying for China — President Trump was quick to reassure the public that "the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security." "People say, 'Is it a threat to have him?' No, it's a threat to lose him," Trump told CNBC shortly after the announcement . But not everyone agrees . Before Huang resigned, the Trump administration's own intelligence officials reportedly identified Alice Huang — the Chinese-born leader of a Southeast Asian company called Megaspeed — as a Chinese intelligence asset who kept in touch with Beijing's top spy agency for more than a year while she targeted the Nvidia chief. Why does this matter? Without government authorization, U.S. export controls prohibit Nvidia from selling certain advanced AI microchips — the chips that have powered the artificial intelligence boom — directly to China, America's main AI competitor. But during a period when Jensen and Alice Huang were seen dining and socializing together , Megaspeed wound up buying billions of dollars' worth of those same Nvidia chips. And Megaspeed not only has ties to Beijing . It's actually under federal investigation for potentially smuggling advanced Nvidia semiconductors out of the U.S. and into China. Jensen Huang during the Nvidia GTC global AI conference in San Jose, Calif., on March 17, 2026. Carlos Barria/Reuters As a result, Huang's reinstatement triggered immediate bipartisan backlash. Outgoing Republican Rep. Don Bacon of Nebraska accused Huang of being "compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy" and said "Nvidia should have moved on" without him. "Congress needs to get to the bottom of who approved high end computer chips sales to China," Bacon wrote on social media . "We cannot say we want to win the AI race and then give China our best technology. We need sunlight on who is responsible." Jensen Huang was compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy. Nvidia should have moved on without Huang and ignored the Administration’s inexplicable desire to save Huang. Congress needs to get to the bottom of who approved high end computer chips sales to China. We cannot say we… — Rep. Don Bacon 🇺🇸✈️🏍️⭐️🎖️ (@RepDonBacon) November 23, 2026 Sen. John Cornyn — another retiring Republican lawmaker — questioned Trump's seemingly cavalier attitude toward Huang and China. "No national security risk?" Cornyn posted . "Based on what?" On Monday, Trump took credit for Huang's return, saying he had spoken directly to Nvidia's board. "I convinced them," the president told CNBC . "I made the deal." The U.S. position on chip sales to China has seesawed over the last 18 months. In April 2025, the Trump administration imposed its first major restrictions on AI semiconductor sales outside the U.S., toughening rules created by the Biden administration. But after several meetings between Trump and Huang — who consistently lobbied for letting chip companies do business with China — the administration eventually approved sales of Nvidia's second-most-powerful chip to Beijing. At the same time, " advisers to Trump told him on at least two occasions that U.S. intelligence had uncovered Ms. Huang's links to the Chinese spy agency and that she was in a close relationship with Mr. Huang while he was still running Nvidia," according to the New York Times . But Trump "downplayed the concerns" and refused to intervene because he "regarded Mr. Huang as a valuable ally and Nvidia as essential to the health of the American economy and stock market," U.S. officials with direct knowledge of the briefings told the paper. Meanwhile, After Jensen stepped down, Trump went on to muse about his return and question whether Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset, denying that anyone in his government had ever told him that. "I don't know that she is a spy," the president told reporters last week . "Usually, what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that's a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she's a spy." On Sunday, Trump called for Huang's return on social media. The New York Times reported that it came after "several days of maneuvering to provide the company's board with assurances that Mr. Huang was not facing criminal charges and did not pose a national security risk." That maneuvering reportedly included directing Vice President JD Vance, who has close ties to Silicon Valley, to speak with both Huang and Nvidia's board. President Trump and Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, interact during the U.S.-Saudi Investment Forum in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 19, 2025. Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters On Monday, the board announced that it had voted unanimously to reinstate Huang. Trump responded by calling Huang "a Great Patriot and National Treasure" and insisting that "the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." In the same post, Trump added that "NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company's compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security." But an internal probe is unlikely to satisfy Congress. Huang is already set to deliver closed-door testimony on Dec. 1 before three congressional committees led by Republicans — and Democrats have signaled that they will keep investigating the issue when they take control of the House and Senate next year. On Monday, Democratic Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona accused Trump of "selling out our national security to keep the stock market high." Another Democrat, Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, said on social media that "this is the greed and lack of accountability that the country just rejected." "There are serious national security concerns being raised about Jensen Huang that should not be papered over by this administration or the Nvidia board," Pritzker added. The president is a significant investor in Nvidia stock. Last week, the Washington Post reported that by August 2026, Trump held a $13 million to $62 million stake in Nvidia — up from as little as $615,000 at the end of 2024. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has also accused the commerce department, led by Howard Lutnick, of stalling efforts by the treasury, defense and state departments, as well as the U.S. trade representative, to block chip sales to Megaspeed. "Commerce has the pen," Bessent said on CNBC earlier this month . "You will have to ask them about their internal processes." Lutnick's former firm Cantor Fitzgerald — now led by his sons — has business relationships with Southeast Asian data centers, leading lawmakers on both sides of the aisle to question "whether Lutnick compromised national security to make money for his family," according to the Guardian . Lutnick should have taken "the threats of communist China more seriously," Republican Sen. Tom Cotton of Arkansas told the Wall Street Journal last week . Congressional Democrats have said they plan to investigate Lutnick in 2027. articles.title: Army will detonate bomb-making material on Wednesday after court clears way
articles.summary: MIDDLETOWN, Iowa (AP) — The U.S. Army plans to detonate bomb-making chemicals in Iowa on Wednesday morning after getting approval from a federal appeals court in a saga that has sowed confusion and included an unusual twist from President Donald Trump. In a statement late Monday, the Army said it’s proceeding with a controlled removal of 68 barrels of lead azide in coordination with state, local and federal authorities. “This is a consensus decision,” acting Army Secretary Adam Telle posted on social media. “Every expert agency agrees, and both Iowa’s current and incoming Governors say the call belongs to the experts.” A three-judge panel of the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals said earlier Monday that the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency adequately incorporated safeguards in an emergency permit to minimize the dispersal of dust. Those conditions address the concerns of environmental groups that sued to stop the detonation, the court said. The court pointed to barriers put up around the area where the barrels are stored along with weather restrictions. It also noted requirements for advance public notification, updated air modeling and environmental monitoring and sampling. The judges said the record also reflected that the Army evaluated “a full range” of alternatives, including using other chemicals to neutralize the lead azide and thermal treatment. In an unusual twist, Trump, commander in chief of the Army, said on social media earlier in the day that in addition to the court's go-ahead, he wanted Gov.-elect Rob Sand to approve the detonation. Sand, a Democrat who doesn't take office until January, has said the decision is fully up to the Trump administration. The blast had been planned for last week The detonation of 68 barrels of lead azide was initially planned for last Friday, but the Army has since changed the date three times following an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects. It said the weather was most favorable this coming Wednesday. Environmentalists sued last week to stop the detonation at the site near Middletown, not far from the Mississippi River about 90 miles (140 km) south of Cedar Rapids. The court temporarily halted the permit, prompting the Army to argue that it didn’t need authorization after all, given that it was an emergency. An attorney for the environmentalists emphasized that their legal challenge centers on the validity of the EPA permit, not the Army’s decision to move forward with the detonation under the emergency provision. Earthjustice managing attorney Rachel Rintelmann said the lawsuit has alerted the public to the threat. “Today, the 8th circuit decided to let the Army proceed with its plan, and we respect that decision," Rintelmann said in a statement Monday. "But the Army created this emergency through neglect, and it owes the people of Iowa more information about the planned detonation and more safeguards for their health.” Incoming governor says the administration should act Sand said in a social media post on Monday that the administration should “make this decision based on the information they have from the people they brought in to do the job months ago and have been on the ground in Middletown for weeks.” On Sunday, Sand posted that because of previous decisions that have already been made, “No good options exist and the situation is more dangerous and unpredictable than it ever should have been.” Current Gov. Kim Reynolds activated the state emergency management office on Friday. The state also created a dedicated website for information about the operation. A flight with Army officials bound for Iowa departed Joint Base Andrews to help support the Army’s planned detonation before Trump’s Truth Social post went out on Monday, two people familiar with the travel arrangements confirmed to the AP. They spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss travel details that had not been made public. Flight tracking websites showed an Army business jet take off from the base just before 1 p.m. Trump posted minutes later. Residents left in limbo as they prepare for detonation Some residents near Middletown have been sealing their windows and doors as a precaution to keep out any lead dust that might result from the detonation. Others who live farther away were raising concern on social media about the possible paths that the plume could take depending on the wind. Officials acknowledge that lead is toxic and have recommended that people stay indoors whenever the detonation happens and clean off outdoor surfaces with water afterward to limit exposure to any lead particles. Middletown Mayor Rodney Johnson said the detonation must take place “so we can move on with our lives.” “Improper storage and disposal is where things go wrong,” he said on social media. Leaders of states that border Iowa also expressed concern. Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe said state agencies are working to establish additional monitoring of air and water quality, public health and agriculture resources. “But I want to emphasize: this is a federal operation,” Kehoe said. “The states of Iowa, Missouri and Illinois do not have a say on when this is conducted." Army says plans are aimed at avoiding something worse In court filings over the weekend, Army Col. Aaron Teller, a munitions emergency response specialist, explained that less liquid inside the barrels means the solution inside is more susceptible to freezing, which increases the sensitivity of the crystals that have formed around the inside of the rim and underside of the lids. “Even a small amount of friction can break the crystal formation, causing an explosive chain reaction,” he said in his declaration to the court. In March, staff at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant found several dozen barrels of degraded lead azide, which is used in munitions production. Crystallization of the material created an unstable and dangerous situation, prompting the Army to assemble experts in munitions chemistry, engineering and environmental safety to come up with a plan. According to EPA documents, alternatives such as neutralizing and decomposing the drums’ contents with other chemicals were considered. But officials said handling the drums would increase the probability of an accidental, fatal detonation. The environmental groups disagreed, arguing in their court filings that other alternatives were not fully considered. Officials contend that the risk of an uncontrolled explosion is growing, particularly as temperatures drop in the coming days. Experts say there are no easy answers Lead azide is “very sensitive” and also susceptible to heat, freezing, shock, friction and “all sorts of things that could cause an accidental detonation,” said John Goodpaster, a chemistry professor at Indiana University, Indianapolis. It’s also old, which increases the risk because explosives become increasingly unstable as they age, he said. Add in the environmental threat caused by the lead that will escape into the atmosphere and the challenge is significant, Goodpaster said. “I do not envy the Army,” Goodpaster said. “They are in a situation where they’ve got a large amount of very dangerous material and not very many good options in terms of trying to dispose of it.” But it’s impossible to predict when it could explode on its own, he said. “The longer we wait, the longer the risk accumulates that they might have an accidental explosion,” Goodpaster said. ___ Montoya Bryan reported from Albuquerque, New Mexico. Associated Press writers Konstantin Toropin in Washington, D.C., Scott Bauer in Madison, Wisconsin, Jacques Billeaud in Phoenix, and Christopher Weber in Los Angeles contributed. articles.title: Jensen Huang is back. Now comes the hard part: Fresh scrutiny in D.C.
articles.summary: Returning Jensen Huang to Nvidia's top job was hailed in Silicon Valley as essential to the future of the AI trade, and on Monday his supporters got their wish. But the embattled CEO's road back to the job may prove easier than the one awaiting him in Washington. Huang's reinstatement comes less than two weeks after revelations of his relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative forced his resignation, setting off a political firestorm over Nvidia's dealings with China and its influence within the Trump administration. Now back atop the company he co-founded more than three decades ago, Huang faces a growing list of congressional inquiries, federal and state scrutiny, and lawmakers on both sides of the aisle demanding answers about whether his relationship compromised US national security. "All the questions that people have been raising in the press and in social media, all those questions are still out there," Martijn Rasser, vice president of technology leadership at the Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP), told Yahoo Finance. "That aspect of the story is still very much in play," said Rasser, a former officer at the Central Intelligence Agency and former director of the technology and national security program at the Center for a New American Security. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang speaks after attending the AI Ecosystem Reception in Tokyo, Japan, on July 16, 2026. (Reuters/Manami Yamada/File Photo) Reuters / REUTERS Nvidia's board of directors said on Monday that the decision to reinstate Huang came after they "received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk." President Trump, who had pushed for Huang's reinstatement since his ouster on Nov. 12, confirmed that he had called the company's board of directors to personally lobby for Huang, telling CNBC that he had been speaking to the board "directly and indirectly" and had offered assurances on national security. The president noted in a Truth Social post that the US government "has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security," and that "the Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." Lawmakers, including prominent members from the president's own party, have disputed those assertions. Republican Sen. John Cornyn, who sits on the Senate Foreign Affairs Committee and the Select Committee on Intelligence, wrote shortly after the news broke Monday, "No national security risk? Based on what?" Republican Representatives Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford wrote in a letter last week requesting Huang's testimony before their respective House committees, saying that "recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information." Democrats made similar calls on Monday, following on prior statements condemning potential national security violations at Nvidia ( NVDA ). "This reckless decision to bring back Jensen Huang does not change the fact that Huang and NVIDIA still owe Congress answers," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, wrote on Monday . "Huang's return only increases the urgency to pass bipartisan export control bills and make sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk." Read more: Thinking of buying Nvidia stock? Consider also buying dozens just like it. In a similar tone to Cornyn, Delaware Democratic Sen. Chris Coons wrote on X , "No national security risk? The guy who was having an affair with a Chinese spy while working relentlessly to help China get access to as many AI chips as possible? Really?" Calls for change at Nvidia came from inside the White House as well, despite the president's statements. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News last week that Nvidia's board needed to "go outside the company" as it searched for a new leader, arguing that the company needed a "dramatic shake-up." Bessent, however, softened his tone in interviews on Sunday. Republicans have also pushed on wider questions surrounding the US government's involvement with Nvidia, including coming congressional interrogations of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whom Huang has called "the person I talk to most in the administration." "If Howard Lutnick wanted my support, perhaps he should have responded to my many letters warning about these Chinese communist front companies and, more importantly, taking the threats of communist China more seriously," Arkansas Sen. Tom Cotton said in an interview with the Wall Street Journal. Nvidia has said in multiple quarterly reports that it projects no compute revenue from China in forward-looking estimates, stating in its fiscal second quarter report, "Under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, we are unable to create and deliver a competitive product for wide distribution in China's data center market with the approval from both the USG and the Chinese government." Huang's first major test will come next week on Dec. 1, when he is scheduled to appear before three House committees investigating his ties to the suspected Chinese operative, Alice Huang, and the potential diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to China. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter is also set to face questioning alongside senior Commerce Department officials responsible for enforcing restrictions on chip exports. An inquiry by the Commerce Department into Singapore-based Megaspeed — the company Alice Huang was once associated with — over alleged violations of US semiconductor export controls was transferred to the Justice Department after Teter asked the Commerce Department for information on the investigation, The New York Times reported." President Trump speaks to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in Washington, D.C., on Sept. 29, 2026. (Reuters/Kevin Lamarque/File Photo) REUTERS / REUTERS Huang has separately agreed to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3, setting up an appearance alongside Lutnick, who has also agreed to testify and is facing scrutiny over reports he slowed investigations into companies suspected of funneling controlled semiconductors into China. Amid a feud with Lutnick that has spilled into public light over the past two weeks, Bessent said investigators would need to ask about any potential export control violations by Nvidia or its customers such as Megaspeed, were they "a low-level fail, was it in the middle, or was it up in the C-suite? Who knew?" The controversy has also drawn investigators beyond Capitol Hill. California's attorney general has subpoenaed Nvidia as part of an investigation connected to Huang's affair. The Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating Nvidia over accounting violations , per Reuters. Proposed national legislation could also present further complications for Nvidia's business. The so-called AI Overwatch Act would tighten export controls on shipments of advanced dual-use AI chips to foreign nations such as China, while the Chip Security Act would impose new verification measures on the locations of chips exported abroad. The Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act would impose more restrictive export controls on the equipment needed to make advanced AI chips. "I think the news of the past few weeks has underscored in the mind of many legislators on Capitol Hill that not enough is being done to ensure that critical US technologies stay out of the hands of our adversaries," SCSP's Rasser told Yahoo Finance. As Huang prepares to appear before Congress, he will have an important ally in Trump, who has repeatedly referred to Huang as a close associate. The president said on Monday that he personally weighed in on the Nvidia board's decision to reinstate Huang and believes his intervention was "very important" to the decision, telling CNBC, "I convinced them." "If I thought he did something wrong, I wouldn't be recommending to his board to hire him," Trump said. Follow Jake Conley on X @byjakeconley or email him at jake.conley@yahooinc.com . articles.title: 死保黄仁勋，马斯克诠释：什么是真正的朋友
articles.summary: 身价万亿的霸总，为了救被赶下台的好兄弟，能拼命到什么程度？在最近这场足以载入史册的硅谷权斗里，马斯克诠释了什么才叫最硬核的“兄弟义气”。 当黄仁勋跌入谷底、被迫辞职时，他没有沉默，没有明哲保身，而是第一时间冲上去，公开开炮力挺！他亲自带头签下超20万人的请愿书，甚至在采访镜头前眼眶泛红、几近落泪，甚至惊动了美国总统亲自出面干预！ 最终，黄仁勋强势回归。他迅速发帖庆祝：“搞定了。” 在这个树倒猢狲散、墙倒众人推的商业世界里，马斯克用行动告诉全世界—— 真正的朋友，不是在你站上巅峰时围着你鼓掌的人，而是在你跌入深渊时，第一个跳下来拉你的人！ 今天咱们就来聊聊，马斯克和英伟达掌门人黄仁勋之间，堪称天花板级别的“神仙友谊”。

articles.title: 老黄“神奇回归” ，投行连夜“撕报告”
articles.summary: 黄仁勋回来了。英伟达董事会在不到两周内完成了一次180度转向——从宣布CEO辞职，到全票通过恢复其职务，整个过程伴随着白宫的直接介入、市场的剧烈震荡，以及华尔街各大投行的连夜重写报告。 11月23日，英伟达宣布黄仁勋即时恢复担任总裁、CEO及董事会成员。消息一出，英伟达股价当日收涨约32%，纳斯达克指数同日涨约7%。 也是这一天，高盛、花旗、瑞银等华尔街大行忙坏了。黄仁勋离职仅约两周，华尔街各大投行的分析师们刚刚完成了一套“无黄仁勋情景”下的估值测算——涵盖各细分行业的预期和估值框架。 复职消息一出，这套东西基本作废，得连夜改回来。 高盛、花旗快速上调估值 高盛在黄仁勋复任后维持英伟达“买入”评级，并给出220美元目标价。 该行在复职当日上午10:01发出报告，英伟达12个月目标价220美元，基于"22倍市盈率乘以标准化每股收益10美元"。按照该行报告，截至11月20日英伟达收盘价为125.53美元，对应目标价隐含上涨空间约75.3%。 报告认为，黄仁勋的愿景、行业影响力和对外协调能力，对英伟达及更广泛的AI产业生态具有重要作用。该行判断，黄仁勋回归将主要强化英伟达既有的企业文化，公司的产品路线图预计仍会按此前计划推进。 不过，高盛同时提醒，管理层交接的不确定性、运营和执行风险、客户订单变化，以及持续进行的内外部调查，仍然构成下行风险。该行还称，美国司法部正在调查英伟达部分客户是否存在出口管制违规，媒体也报道SEC正在调查英伟达此前披露的部分事项。 花旗的调整更为积极。 复职当日上午10:43，花旗将英伟达目标价从225美元上调至240美元，评级维持买入。 该行表示，"在我们看来，此次复职消除了CEO过渡所带来的核心压制因素。"理由包括：产品路线图、客户关系和供应商合作关系的连续性得以恢复，领导层风险下降。目标倍数因此从"约14倍FY28E每股收益"上调至"约15倍FY28E每股收益"。 花旗预计英伟达FY27至FY29的核心每股收益分别为9.60美元、16.05美元和20.47美元。 从“关键人风险”到“信心修复”，瑞银：供应链估值可能获得修复 瑞银在11月23日发布的报告中，将黄仁勋复任称为“明确的利好”，并维持英伟达买入评级和220美元目标价。 瑞银认为，黄仁勋辞任期间，市场主要担忧三件事：融资安排、供应链战略以及人才留存。随着其回归，这些不确定性“应该会有所减弱”。 除了英伟达本身，该行还将影响范围扩大到AI硬件供应链。该行此前判断，黄仁勋重新出任CEO，有望恢复投资者对AI交易的信心，并推动存储、光学和模拟芯片供应商的估值修复。相关供应商此前几周经历了明显估值压缩。 英伟达还拥有规模庞大的产业链承诺。报告提到，公司目前约有3900亿美元供应承诺，因此即使英伟达希望减少对生态系统的融资支持，实际操作空间也可能有限。 该行将220美元目标价维持不变，估值依据为2028财年预期每股收益18.80美元，以及约12倍的市盈率。以报告所列价格计算，瑞银预计英伟达股价仍有约30%的升值空间，预期总回报约为30.7%。 不过，该行并未认为所有问题都已解决。报告指出，数据中心建设所涉及的土地、电力和基础设施问题仍然存在，尤其是在美国总统特朗普持续反对企业在美国以外建设数据中心的情况下。 汇丰：维持持有，目标价170美元 汇丰的态度最为保守。复职当日，该行维持英伟达持有评级，目标价170美元（现价约125.53美元）。 该行指出，这是一次"急转弯"——董事会主席11月17日还明确表示无意复任，六天后却一致投票恢复其职务。 该行目标价170美元对应约35%的上行空间，按其评级规则通常超过20%应给买入，但报告维持持有，折射出对调查进展和政策风险的持续谨慎。 摩根大通没有“撕掉”看空报告 与高盛、花旗和瑞银相比，摩根大通并未因为黄仁勋回归改变立场。 摩根大通维持英伟达“减持”观点。该行认为，股价上涨更接近一场“缓解性反弹”，并不意味着信用风险已经下降。 报告指出，市场对AI建设的信心，仍然“很大程度上建立在黄仁勋个人身上”，包括他与客户及华盛顿的关系，以及是否愿意动用英伟达资产负债表支持芯片采购方。 这意味着，黄仁勋回归可能重新增强英伟达为客户提供融资、担保或其他交易支持的可能性。对股权投资者而言，这有助于稳定AI建设预期；但对债权投资者而言，英伟达承担更多生态融资责任，也可能意味着资产负债表风险增加。 该行同时强调，英伟达仍面临多个未解决问题，包括独立调查、出口管制审查以及未来融资承诺的不确定性。该行认为，英伟达现金流和资产负债表足以吸收短期波动，但投资级科技、媒体和电信债券市场中仍存在相对更具吸引力的标的。 报告最后维持原有结论：英伟达“仍然处在风险尚未完全消退的阶段”。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 从对冲工具沦为流动性来源，大宗商品抛售潮触底了么？
articles.summary: 大宗商品本应是动荡中的避风港，结果却成了被抛售的资产。 近日，高盛大宗商品BCOM指数旗下无一板块幸免，贵金属与能源各自在20日内下跌约14%。该行大宗商品交易台在最新一期《每周大宗商品思考》（ Weekly Commodity Thoughts ）中写道： 又是疯狂的一周！大宗商品遭受了两轮连续冲击——先是美联储鹰派立场和强美元重新定价推高了实际利率，随后AI股票去杠杆化强制触发了大宗商品的全面清仓，与美元走势无关。BCOM各板块无一幸免。 这轮抛售最值得关注的特征，是它与基本面几乎毫无关系。 高盛指出， 最拥挤的持仓跌得最惨——而且往往没有具体利空消息触发。 英国碳排放配额仓位处于过去三年的第98百分位，单周下跌10%；糖价仓位处于第92百分位，叠加巴西雷亚尔贬值，单周跌去8%。 这是典型的流动性驱动抛售 ：不是因为这些商品的供需出了问题，而是因为持有它们的人需要在别处补充保证金。 贵金属和能源板块在过去20天内各自下跌约14%。当下，反弹是否临近？交易员Quinn的标准差信号说是；但CTA模型说系统性卖盘尚未结束。 铜：三重压力同时袭来 铜单周下跌10%，三重压力同时袭来：全球经济增长担忧（BCOM整体跌5%）、亚洲需求悲观，以及美国可能出口铜的预期引发上期所大规模做空。 高盛团队坦承判断失误： 我们的失误在于，低估了贸易商将金属转道亚洲以填补缺口的便利程度，以及某亚洲大国市场对需求的悲观情绪有多深。我们认为美国自2024年1月以来已超额进口170万吨，吸收了全球过剩量，但近期（小规模）出口已向市场证明存在'泄压阀'，在需求低迷的环境下，这令人不安。 与此同时，高盛表示，中国实物铜市场是"我们15年来见过的最紧张状态"，现货升水高达750美元/吨，上期所期货曲线呈现倒挂，国内库存同比下降70%。 但这些都没能支撑铜价。该行说道： "这样的紧张局面，充其量只是价格的边缘因素。" 黄金：有序的清仓，CTA仍在卖出 黄金较年内高点已下跌34%，刚刚经历了3月以来最差的一周。 高盛强调，这轮抛售与1月份的混乱截然不同： 与1月相比，此次抛售有序得多，整体持仓较为均衡，贵金属在高利率、科技股下跌的环境中未能发挥避险作用。我们的CTA模型显示，尽管已经持有大量空头仓位，在平盘或下跌的行情中仍有进一步卖出空间（仅在价格急涨时会有小幅回补）。ETF持仓依然高企，众所周知，但出乎意料地具有粘性。 换句话说， 趋势追踪者已经做空，且除非金价大幅反弹，否则还会继续卖。 仅周五一天，上期所黄金持仓就减少了8500手，属于近三年单日降幅的第95百分位。 唯一的亮点是印度和土耳其实物需求的回升。但高盛自身的黄金Delta头寸维持"小幅做空至中性"——"因为黄金目前仍未能找到支撑"。 对于何时反弹的问题，目前分歧明显。该行交易员Robert Quinn此前发出了"4-5个标准差"的恐慌信号，历史上这类信号通常在一周内出现反转。但CTA模型显示系统性卖盘尚未结束。 从更长周期看，高盛研究团队在2027年展望报告《又是2022年》中预计，随着美联储继续加息，黄金近期面临下行压力和高波动，但结构性央行购金将推动金价在2027年底升至4650美元，一旦降息开始，2028年底可达5600美元。 原油：市场学会了对冲突视而不见 原油本周同样承压。中美俄会议被解读为局势不会立即升级，油价随之下滑；周四有消息称华盛顿正在考虑新一轮打击行动，且伊朗表示若船只遭袭将予以回应，油价有所回升。 但高盛表示："实际上，任何反弹都被更广泛的宏观疲软所压制。" 实物市场似乎找到了底部，远期升贴水（DFL）本周基本持平，北海实物差价略有回升。 最值得关注的是波动率结构：已实现波动率大幅收窄，但隐含波动率在整条曲线上依然偏高，交易员正将近端头寸滚动至6-12个月区间。12个月布伦特波动率处于三年历史的第100百分位，而12个月25-delta看跌期权偏斜仅处于第8百分位。 高盛认为这是一个做反向操作的机会： 我们预计已实现波动率的收窄将持续，因为近期打击行动真正造成供应中断的可能性正在降低。 市场似乎愿意对冲突视而不见，只要石油持续流动。美国政府的表态也越来越倾向于将打击风险推迟至近期之后——上周末，特朗普在福克斯新闻中被引述称，如果新年前没有达成协议，他倾向于在新年后打击伊朗。 尽管如此，我们倾向于通过买入近端价差期权来对冲做空波动率的风险，以防范升级驱动的反弹。 TTF天然气：人人持有期权，市场极度做空Gamma 高盛大宗商品联席交易主管Jon Yarrow在该行天然气展望电话会议上解释了为何欧洲天然气自10月突破2022年高点以来如此剧烈震荡： 期权市场的未平仓合约规模在几个方面都不寻常：第一，几乎每个行权价的持仓都非常大——从约40欧元一直到125欧元——尤其是12月合约；第二，今年只有几次隐含波动率看起来相对已实现波动率偏低，这可能意味着很多人持有这些期权是方向性的、持仓到期的……如果做市商在卖出波动率……他们就需要对冲Delta。另一方面，那些买入期权、持仓到期的人，使得市场极度做空Gamma。 10月的涨势在100欧元之前"异常有序"，但随后"买盘不够，暴力就来了"。 冬季供需平衡依然偏紧，但两股力量正在反向发力：霍尔木兹海峡流量在回升，且1月JKM（日韩基准价）基差极弱，"亚洲在1月份不一定想要实物天然气"。 Yarrow对于是否已经见顶持谨慎态度："当右侧尾部风险仍然存在时，现在做空市场是否为时过早？"他认为第一季度"作为基准情景将高度波动"，最终走势取决于天气和时机。 但一旦卡塔尔新增产能投产，结论就清晰了： 假设供应恢复到合理程度，明年夏天的储气不会有任何问题。即便价格再低15欧元，也并不真正存在短缺。然后，这就开始将我们引向长期的看空交易。 清仓先行，基本面其后 把这一切拼在一起：这一周发生的事情，与大宗商品本身关系不大。 中国铜市场的极度紧张、央行持续购金、原油实物市场的支撑——这些都败给了实际利率上升和AI股票的去杠杆化。大宗商品在2026年大部分时间里被当作战争对冲工具来交易，而过去这一周则表明，当股票保证金追缴到来时，它们同样会被当作流动性来源。 高盛研究团队警告，即便在基准情景下，黄金也面临"近期下行压力和波动率上升……因为美联储继续加息"。 反弹是否临近？Quinn的标准差信号说是；CTA模型说系统性卖盘尚未结束。只要AI股票的下跌没有找到底部，大宗商品大概率还要继续等待。 而"实物资产"的交易，可能要等到降息周期开启之后才能真正站稳。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 豆包推出“小豆”，大厂争夺个人AI入口
articles.summary: Personal Agent的竞争正在升温。 11月24日，豆包旗下AI个人助理产品“小豆”正式开启公测，采用独立App的产品形态。目前，小豆采取邀请制开放，用户凭邀请码即可开启体验。 与豆包App不同，小豆更加侧重长期记忆、主动服务及任务执行能力，应用场景覆盖办公、消费、出行等个人事务。 豆包表示，未来小豆上的能力与体验也将逐步在豆包App上线。 华尔街见闻·全天候科技第一时间获得了小豆的邀请码，并进行体验。 对于此前使用过豆包和豆包工作的用户而言，可以直接将这当中沉淀的记忆导入小豆，无需重新介绍自己的职业背景、工作习惯及个人偏好等。 小豆还提供了多个第三方应用的连接入口，包括高德地图、Wind、自如、百度网盘等，覆盖金融、出行、居住及办公等场景。 在完成Wind的连接后，全天候科技尝试让小豆将英伟达最近两个交易日的行情数据整理成Excel文件，小豆随即完成了数据查询及文件生成。 从实际体验来看，小豆的整个任务执行流程更加自动化，用户无需了解具体的工具调用方式，仅通过自然语言即可完成操作。 这一变化在生活服务场景中更加明显。比如全天候科技向小豆提出了一个较为模糊的需求：“能帮我看一下我抖音买的那个券现在是否有降价？” 在没有进一步提供商户名称及商品信息的情况下，小豆查询了笔者在抖音的历史订单，找到了此前实付400元购买的500元代金券，并与商户当前售价进行比对，给出了暂未降价的结论。 类似的需求还可以通过设置定时任务的方式交由小豆持续跟进。 这也成为当前多家科技大厂争相突破的方向。 今年9月，Meta推出Personal Agent产品Muse。Meta创始人兼CEO扎克伯格在10月21日举行的三季度业绩会上透露，美国和加拿大已有超过1000万用户完成MusePersonal Agent的设置。 国内互联网大厂也在加紧布局。 10月13日，阿里推出Personal Agent“千问Go！”，依托阿里旗下的商业生态及开放平台，将服务进一步延伸至购物保价、保险理赔等场景。 10月27日，蚂蚁集团发布灵光2.0，将其定位为能够处理个人事务的AI助理。 豆包的入局也已引起同行关注。一位接近蚂蚁集团的人士向全天候科技透露，灵光内部已将小豆视为潜在的竞争对手。 相比于通用AI助手，Personal Agent有望为互联网大厂带来更高的用户黏性。 过去，用户可以根据不同大模型的能力，在多个AI应用之间灵活切换。但随着个人记忆、应用授权及自动化任务不断沉淀，更换AI产品的成本也可能随之提高。 即便不同AI产品在模型能力上逐渐趋同，其基于个人数据和服务生态所提供的体验仍有可能形成较大差异。 但Personal Agent的竞争并不只发生在App内部。 对于需要感知用户状态、主动提供服务的Personal Agent而言，作为用户日常使用频率最高的智能终端之一，手机也是一个重要的竞争阵地。 11月23日，荣耀发布了搭载YOYO·豆包手机助手的荣耀700系列。借助此次推出的AI灵动背屏，用户可以通过语音交互完成个性化背屏定制等操作，并体验英语陪练等功能。 与此同时，荣耀自身也在持续加码Personal Agent。 今年9月，荣耀发布MagicOS 11，将智能体执行框架进一步下沉至操作系统层面，系统级智能体YOYO仍是荣耀串联各类AI能力的重要入口。 这使得互联网大厂与手机厂商在Personal Agent领域的关系变得更加微妙。 手机厂商掌握着操作系统、硬件传感器及系统服务能力，在感知用户需求、跨应用执行及跨设备协同等方面具有天然优势；互联网大厂则拥有长期积累的用户数据、模型能力及丰富的互联网服务生态。 双方存在较大的互补空间，但也都希望成为用户调动各类服务的第一入口。 对于豆包而言，推出独立的个人助理产品，可以进一步沉淀用户记忆、拓宽服务生态；与手机厂商展开合作，则有望拓展AI能力触达用户的场景。 随着越来越多的玩家入局，Personal Agent的竞争正在从单一的模型能力比拼，演变为一场围绕个人记忆、服务生态及终端入口的综合较量。 过去，互联网大厂争夺的是用户打开App之后的时间。如今，它们开始争夺用户打开App之前的需求。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 对冲失效，空头止损，杠杆ETF狂扫410亿！复盘老黄回归，美股“惊心动魄”的一天
articles.summary: 黄仁勋复职，触发美股史诗级逼仓，但野村警告：机械性反弹解决不了结构性问题。 当地时间周一，英伟达董事会宣布黄仁勋重返总裁兼CEO职位，这份措手不及的新闻稿彻底引爆了此前已蓄势待发的机械性买盘。 野村证券跨资产策略师Charlie McElligott在当日最新报告中，将这场反弹定性为多重机制的叠加引爆： 看跌期权对冲头寸失效、空头被迫止损、趋势型基金翻多。 他以一句话概括全天行情： 对冲头寸消亡，空头遭遇止损，标普狂飙，追逐上行。 与此同时，野村测算， 杠杆ETF在当日收盘前的被动再平衡买入规模高达410亿美元，为有史以来第二大单日买入。 然而，McElligott同时警示，机械性反弹无法消除宏观层面的结构性压力： 金融条件仍在收紧，美联储未有任何鸽派转向，而更深层的资产配置者"退出"风险依然悬而未决。 恐慌有多深：上周抹去的市值与财富效应警报 此次反弹的前提，是过去数周市场极度恶化后蓄积的反弹能量。 上周标普500指数单周跌幅达8.6%，为去年关税风波以来最差单周表现；纳斯达克100指数单周下挫10%，创2020年3月以来最大周跌幅；英伟达当周下跌23%，为2008年10月以来最大周跌幅；VIX恐慌指数一度突破40，为2025年4月以来首次。 高盛经济学家估算，今年以来金融条件累计收紧约100个基点，仅上周一周便贡献逾40个基点。 高盛Tony Pasquariello统计，英伟达一只个股在六周内市值蒸发2.7万亿美元。 McElligott阐释逻辑称：当股票市场成为美国经济金融条件松紧的核心传导机制时，当局只有在事态真正恶化后才会出手，且出手方向必然偏向"推升财富效应"。 美国家庭持有的股票资产规模接近GDP的200%，意味着股市每下跌10%，家庭财富将损失相当于GDP约20%的价值。 McElligott据此认为，这解释了为何政治层面对此次市场暴跌作出直接干预。 值得注意的是，此次"救市"并无降息、量化宽松或流动性互换，只有一位在任总统亲自与上市公司董事会沟通，以及华盛顿为一位CEO背书的国家安全认定。高盛的Anton Tran对此评论称： 尚不确定市场命运几乎等同于一个人的命运，究竟是好事还是坏事。 美股暴涨的第一阶段：波动率骤降引发逼空，对冲头寸加速归零 此次大涨的第一个机械驱动力，来自衍生品市场的结构性逼仓。 据McElligott在上周四报告中的铺垫，彼时期权做市商处于2019年以来最大净空头Gamma敞口，大量客户持有的认沽期权形成巨额空头Delta， 一旦隐含波动率停止上升，做市商将被迫买回此前卖出的期货对冲头寸。周一，这一机制被强制触发。 据野村当日盘中数据，VIX下跌7个点至28.9，纳斯达克100上涨6.7%；VIX近月期货下跌4.4个点至24.1；纳斯达克隐含波动率VXN骤降9.7个点至35.5；波动率的波动率指标VVIX暴跌20点至118。 标普500指数直接突破每日跨式期权上沿，做市商被迫大规模回购期货，形成纯粹的机械式买盘。 与此同时，空头损伤惨重。据高盛John Flood的资金流向报告，对冲基金上周以四年多来最大规模重新建立总敞口，以宏观产品做空为主，多空比例降至有记录以来最低。与此同时， 英伟达3倍做空ETP在盘前开市后数秒内暴跌逾91%。 值得注意的是，尽管恐慌情绪明显缓解，VVIX仍比其与VIX的一年期历史关系高出逾6个点，处于过去21年93百分位；VIX本身在标普500单日上涨5%的背景下报28.9，处于过去37年91百分位。 McElligott由此提示，市场的恐惧尚未完全消散。 第二阶段：趋势追踪资金翻多门槛被穿越，CTA模型触发回补 第二轮机械买盘来自系统性趋势追踪策略（CTA）的被动轧平。 据野村模型，标普500指数收于7043点以上，将触发12个月信号窗口从净空头转为接近平仓，该窗口权重占模型总权重的46%，单独触发的回补规模为161亿美元，纳斯达克100同步触发约24亿美元回补。 在全球股票期货层面，+4%的冲击下模型需买入约340亿美元。 周一标普500开盘于7227点，该触发位已在开盘之初被有效穿越，前提是指数在收盘前维持在该水平上方。 据Zerohedge统计，与上周四的野村估算相比，触发规模明显扩大——彼时+4%情景对应的全球买入量为211亿美元，现已增至336亿美元。原因在于，周四和周五两日大跌将标普信号从轻度空头推至最大空头， 卖出越深，回补规模越大 。 高盛模型同样印证这一逻辑：截至上周五，CTA在过去一个月抛售570亿美元后，净空美股约190亿美元，且在所有情景下均为净卖出；高盛设定的长期翻多阈值7119点也已在开盘时被穿越。 然而，穿越7043点仅意味着标普信号从-100%回升至-8%，趋势追踪资金仅是轧平，而非转多。 若要使其重新建立净多头，模型需要7625点，完全建仓则在7710点附近。从当日开盘位至7625点之间逾5%的涨幅空间，仍需依赖其他买家承接。 第三阶段：杠杆ETF形成410亿美元收盘再平衡买盘 周一最具压倒性的被动买盘来自杠杆ETF的收盘再平衡机制。 这类产品天然形成"越涨越买"的负Gamma结构，需在每日收盘前完成再平衡买入。 野村实时预测显示，周一收盘再平衡买入总规模约410亿美元，其中科技股约167亿美元、半导体约128亿美元、"科技七巨头"约42亿美元、标普500相关产品约41亿美元，全部处于野村证券历史数据库的100百分位，即有记录以来最大量级。 在超过5100个交易日的回溯历史中，仅有一次买入再平衡规模更大，即2025年4月9日关税暂停当日的465亿美元。 据高盛ETF业务负责人Chris Lucas的数据，尽管纳斯达克100指数在33个交易日内下跌近20%，杠杆ETF同期仍录得200亿美元净流入，零售投资者一路加杠杆抄底，造就了今日这批百亿美元级别的被动买家。McElligott两周前测算时，该复合体总规模已达1515亿美元。 Zerohedge汇总McElligott的三阶段框架，粗略估算如下：410亿美元杠杆ETF买盘，叠加最多约340亿美元CTA回补，扣除波动率控制基金因单日波动过大被迫减仓的100至160亿美元，在任何主动型投资者作出决策之前，市场已存在约600亿美元净被动买盘。 反弹是终点还是起点：三个条件仍差两个 尽管这场机械式反弹烈度罕见，多数策略师对其可持续性持保守态度。 高盛策略师Ben Snider认为，标普500的真正底部需要三个条件同时具备：一是能够重建AI盈利信心的催化剂，二是更宽松的宏观背景（如美联储发出鸽派信号），三是仓位的大幅出清。 按此框架，三个条件周一只满足了半个多 ：AI催化剂由白宫直接提供；仓位方面，对冲基金已大幅减仓，但据高盛Lee Coppersmith的数据，其他机构投资者仓位仍偏高，德意志银行策略师Parag Thatte将主动型投资者仓位列于第4百分位，整体仓位处于第11百分位，尚未出现全面抛售；而鸽派美联储毫无踪影，市场目前仍将12月加息列为近确定性事件，高盛预计3月将再度加息，标普500单日上涨5%反而在客观上松动了此前替代美联储发挥紧缩功能的金融条件。 历史基率同样提示谨慎。 根据德意志银行Thatte的研究，一旦此类波动率冲击发生，历史上波动率平息和股市筑底通常需要六至八周，标普500在非衰退情形下平均还会再跌14%至16%。 摩根大通市场情报团队周一将立场调整为战术性谨慎，以2018年底为参照——当年感恩节反弹被一路卖出直至平安夜。 McElligott本人也对这场机械反弹的信号意义明确划定边界："这次'机械性反弹'对于我此前讨论的更长期'结构性力量'不提供任何保证"，包括金融条件收紧、AI资本支出预期下调对经济增长的负面冲击，以及通胀仍偏高迫使政策维持紧缩取向。 他的框架指向一个更根本的问题：在过去十五年"逢跌买入"条件反射与近期"保住本金"范式转换之间，大型资产配置者最终将倒向哪一边。这个答案，不在周一的收盘单里。 articles.title: 刚刚，Anthropic内部Claude模型独立攻克代数版P/NP问题，全篇Lean机器验证通过
articles.summary: Anthropic的内部研究版Claude模型，刚刚独立证明了代数版本的P对NP猜想。 论文的唯一作者署名就是Claude， GitHub： https://github.com/anthropics/formal-math/tree/main/vp-vnp paper： https://www.alphaxiv.org/pdf/2611.vp-vnp-arithmetic-lower-bounds 不过整项成果没有经过人类数学家的人工审稿，但已经用形式化验证工具Lean 4完成了端到端的机器证明与检验。 这篇论文的核心结论只有一个：在任意域上，VP都不等于VNP。 这个结论正式回答了理论计算机科学界悬置数十年的Valiant猜想。 为了让大家理解它到底证明了什么，我们需要先回到线性代数里的一个经典概念。 对于一个2乘2的矩阵，行列式的计算公式是ad减去bc。 如果把中间的减号改成加号，变成ad加上bc，在数学上就叫做永久式。 当矩阵维度扩大到13乘13甚至更大时，行列式和永久式的展开式都会迅速膨胀到几十亿项。 但是计算行列式有高斯消元法这样的快捷方式，可以在多项式时间内迅速算出结果。 那么永久式有没有类似的捷径？ 学术界一直猜想它绝对没有。这篇论文给出了确凿的下界证明：在实数域以及任何特征不为2的域上，任何计算m乘m矩阵永久式的算术电路，门数量必然大于m的c倍log m的三分之一次方，其中c是一个大于0的常数。 对于哈密顿回路多项式，这个超多项式下界在任意特征的域上全部成立。 这意味着，无论是永久式还是哈密顿回路多项式，都不可能被多项式规模的算术电路计算出来。 在理论计算机科学中，多项式规模算术电路能计算的家族称为VP，而永久式和哈密顿回路多项式所在的家族称为VNP。论文的结论直接给出了VP是VNP的真子集，彻底分开了这两个复杂度类。 同时，论文还将这一结论推广到了带逼近计算的边界复杂度。哪怕算术电路被允许通过形式劳伦级数进行逼近计算，VNP依然无法被包含在VP的闭包之中。 论文的论证结构非常清晰，主要分为平坦情况与收缩情况两大分支。 证明过程中没有直接硬啃永久式，而是将其转化为网络连通性相关的多项式，或者包含加权停机分支的通用自动机多项式。 在第一种平坦情况下，欧几里得距离能够代表张量的谱点距离，团队利用完全图上的布线网络，结合平衡分割点的张量秩性质，直接推导出超多项式门数量下界。 在第二种收缩情况下，几何距离表现出收缩性质，可以推导出一类庞加莱不等式，并进一步转化为树状网络的重布线规律。随后通过一步对角化论证，证明了如果永久式存在小尺寸算术电路，就能构造出自我矛盾的加速器程序，从而完成反证。 这两个分支覆盖了所有可能的数学域，最终得出统一的下界。 需要划清界限的是，这项成果虽然解决了代数领域的VP对VNP问题，但并没有解决经典的图灵机P对NP猜想。 算术电路要求所有加法和乘法步骤对域内的所有元素以及扩域元素一律通用，不能专门针对0和1这两个离散数值做针对性的位操作逻辑。布尔电路则完全不受这个代数规则的约束。因此，关于布尔电路与图灵机的核心猜想P对NP，目前依然处于未决状态。 但对AI领域而言，震撼的地方在于整个研究的推进方式。 这篇论文完全由AI发现并由AI撰写，相关命题和推理步骤全部转换成了Lean 4代码，只依赖Mathlib标准库和标准公理，代码仓库已经公开，全程通过了Lean编译器的严格形式化检查。 写在最后 这篇论文回答了一个人类追问了几十年的本质问题： 面对宇宙中一类极其复杂的计算任务，我们到底能不能找到偷懒的万能算法？ 论文给出的铁证回答是：绝对不可能。 用大白话讲，它在理论上直接堵死了一大批人对奇迹算法的幻想，它的现实意义主要在这四件事上： 1. 宣判一类计算问题不存在捷径 在计算机领域，算矩阵的行列式很简单，电脑一瞬间就能算出来。 但是只要把公式里的一个减号改成加号，变成永久式，哪怕矩阵只有几十乘以几十，让全地球所有的超级计算机算到宇宙毁灭，用常规方法也算不完。 几十年来，全世界的大批顶尖学者都在猜：是不是我们太笨了，其实存在某种极其巧妙的运算法则，能像算行列式一样瞬间算出永久式？ 这篇论文彻底断了这个念想。它用严密的代数证明了：只要你只用加减乘除这套规则，任何算法所需要的计算步骤，都会随着数据规模爆炸式增长，永远不可能有省时省力的快速捷径。 后来的科学家再也不用在这个死胡同里浪费生命了。 2. 给当代密码学吃下了一颗关键的定心丸 你每天都在用的银行转账、手机支付、微信聊天加密，之所以绝对安全，底层逻辑只有一个：破解这些密码的计算量大到无法想象，现有的计算机在人类寿命范围内根本算不完。 但是密码学家其实一直很恐慌：万一哪天突然蹦出一个天才算法，把这些原本看似不可能的难题瞬间解开了怎么办？那样全球的加密系统瞬间就会全部报废。 这篇论文在代数层面上，给这种安全体系铸了一道极硬的铁壁。它严格证明了某些核心问题在代数结构上确实存在不可跨越的计算壁垒，直接巩固了现代密码学的理论地基。 3. 未来算力优化出路 既然论文证明了精确解题不可能有捷径，那所有搞计算机算法的人就必须彻底死心，把方向转向更务实的领域： 既然求绝对精准的答案会把计算机累死，以后的算力研究就只能专注在近似计算、概率算法或者专用启发式算法上。 这就好比物理学家证明了永动机不可能造出来，工程师们才不再去妄想永动机，转而去全力死磕如何把内燃机和电池的效率提高百分之几。 4. 摸到了P对NP门槛 全世界悬赏最高的数学难题，就是价值百万美元的P对NP问题，它本质上问的是：所有能被快速检验答案的问题，能不能被快速求解？ 这个问题人类硬啃了几十年，几乎连从哪里下刀都不知道，到处都是思维死角。 而这篇论文解决的VP对VNP问题，就是P对NP在代数世界的平行投射，也是人类目前公认攻克P对NP的最重要也是唯一有希望的前哨战。 搞清楚了代数世界里的计算极限，人类才算真正看清了这堵高墙的真实轮廓，为最终解决终极计算极限问题拆掉了最大的一块绊脚石。# 本文来源： AI寒武纪 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 英伟达一夜暴涨31%，空头跌懵了
articles.summary: 英伟达股价周一单日飙升逾31%，将押注其下跌的空头打了个措手不及——杠杆做空产品最高暴跌92%，空头单日账面亏损约112亿美元。 触发这场轧空行情的，是英伟达董事会宣布恢复黄仁勋首席执行官职务。消息一出，英伟达股价当日最高涨幅达37%，收盘报165.05美元，涨幅31.5%，市值单日增加约9500亿美元。据ORTEX联合创始人Peter Hillerberg向MarketWatch透露，这是美国股市历史上单只股票单日市值增幅最大的一次。 对于此前顺势做空的交易员而言，这一逆转来得格外猛烈。英伟达上周累计下跌23%，本月截至上周五跌幅达39%，做空者一度坐拥丰厚浮盈。然而黄仁勋复职的消息在数小时内彻底扭转了局面。 据ORTEX数据，英伟达空头周一单日账面亏损约112亿美元，是2019年以来最惨烈的单日亏损，"超过此前最差单日亏损的两倍以上"，Peter Hillerberg表示。 周一的亏损已将空头上周积累的全部利润一笔抹去。不过Hillerberg指出，自10月29日以来，空头整体仍处于约150亿美元的盈利状态。 杠杆做空产品遭重创，最高跌92% 对于使用杠杆做空产品的交易员，冲击更为剧烈。 在美国市场，寻求提供英伟达单日表现两倍反向回报的GraniteShares 2x Short NVDA Daily ETF（代码NVD）单日暴跌63%。据彭博报道，这只规模约1亿美元的基金此前受益于英伟达的持续下跌，截至上周五今年累计涨幅达46%。 欧洲市场的损失更为惨重。GraniteShares 3x Short NVIDIA Daily ETP（代码3SNV）单日暴跌92%，Leverage Shares旗下同类产品（代码NV3S）下跌80%。 与此同时，做多方向的杠杆产品则迎来暴涨。GraniteShares 2x Long NVDA Daily ETF（代码NVDL）单日飙升约62%。 “安全气囊”机制避免产品归零 尽管跌幅触目惊心，两款欧洲产品均未被迫清盘，内置的风控机制发挥了作用。 据彭博报道，理论上，若标的股票单日涨幅超过33%，三倍做空产品在敞口不变的情况下将面临彻底清零的风险。Leverage Shares通讯与策略主管Oktay Kavrak表示，NV3S在交易过程中暂停约15分钟，重新计算敞口后恢复交易，"安全气囊机制做到了它该做的事：在极端行情下切断了彻底归零的风险。" GraniteShares创始人兼CEO Will Rhind则表示，3SNV采用"止损"功能防止产品归零，"正因为有止损机制，3SNV得以继续存续，而不必被迫关闭。" 杠杆产品的结构性风险再度警示市场 此次事件再度揭示了单一股票杠杆产品的内在风险。据彭博报道，这类产品通常使用衍生品，并每日重置风险敞口，意味着较长时期的回报可能与所标示的倍数大相径庭。它们是交易工具，而非传统的买入并持有型投资。 值得注意的是，截至周一，GraniteShares的NVDL和NVD两款产品今年以来均录得逾40%的亏损，而英伟达股票本身年初至今跌幅仅约11%。 Bloomberg Intelligence高级ETF策略师Eric Balchunas对MarketWatch直言："不管是被清盘还是重置，都改变不了你刚刚跌了90%这个事实。这就是一场清洗——如果你持有这类产品，你基本上什么都没了。" WallachBeth Capital的ETF董事总经理Mohit Bajaj则表示："任何杠杆ETF都存在风险，同时也伴随着潜在回报。交易员必须确保密切监控持仓。" Roundhill Financial首席投资策略师Drew Pettit也指出："这就是在高波动环境下做空某样东西的危险所在。" 此次行情也令市场联想起2018年2月5日的"波动率末日"（Volmageddon）事件——彼时CBOE波动率指数（VIX）单日翻倍，多款做空波动率产品遭到清盘。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
